title: Nvidia is preparing to oust Jensen Huang
titleZh: Nvidia is preparing to oust Jensen Huang
author: jbredeche
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: Topfi
comments.textRawHtml:
I recently recalled Nvidia's rather strange reaction to the Gamers Nexus investigation into GPU smuggling [0]. Found it somewhat strange at the time how incredibly agitated the reaction seemed to have been, given Nvidia could sell the same GPUs for the same price essentially instantly without the Chinese market. Their reaction wasn't merely a denial, dismissal or even silence, but very irrationally sounding for a company of their size and standing.

Why not just sell to not-sanctioned entities, ensure compliance to the best of your abilities and otherwise keep your head down? Again, wasn't like they struggled to find buyers for their chips.

Considering Megaspeed, I now see this in a very different light. Him cheating is personal and I wish the affected members of any family of a cheater the best, but not relevant for us outsiders.

Being honey trapped very bad securities wise, but he'd be a victim (and evidence for why we shouldn't discount Mistral in the frontier lab race [1]). If sanctions avoidance went all the way to the top, that is hard to negate even for a board that is interested in keeping him. At that stage he was neither honey trapped nor "merely horny"...

[0] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1H3xQaf7BFI

[1] https://time.com/archive/7146565/hollandes-popularity-goes-u...

children.author: ksec
children.textRawHtml:
This is the same as asking Apple to ignore Chinese market, when China has more active iPhone user than the whole US population.

I am not entirely sure I buy the Spy thesis. And Alice's husband knew this all along. Which makes the whole thing more doggy.

And Jensen's view isn't wrong. There is no way you could contain China via import restrictions. Not when they are the second-largest economy and still rapidly advancing. There are better ways to handle this, one huge ban isn't one.

But I wholeheartedly disagree with ousting Jensen. And given the timing of all these releases, I wouldn't be surprised someone inside the government wants to bring him down.

children.author: aurareturn
children.textRawHtml:
But I wholeheartedly disagree with ousting Jensen. And given the timing of all these releases, I wouldn't be surprised someone inside the government wants to bring him down.
I think there are a lot of people who want to bring him down. His competition - AMD, Broadcom, Google. OpenAI and Anthropic also have advocated for banning chip exports to China because of Chinese lab LLM competition. Then there are both Republican and Democrats who likely support the views of OpenAI/Anthropic.

Finally, because he's of Han Chinese origin, I bet they thought they could get the media to coordinate a narrative around him that will force him out. Of course, he sort of made it easy to pin something on him.

There are a lot of Game of Thrones going on in AI. Everyone is jockeying. Everyone has different incentives. Super high stakes game.

children.author: svara
children.textRawHtml:
The thing is that at this point, even if this was all a plot to take him down, it worked! Can't go back to the information not being public.

He's operating in a highly charged political environment in which his credibility is a key asset. He can't effectively advocate for NVIDIA's interests if his credibility is damaged.

And this goes directly to his credibility on the most politically charged issue of all: The geopolitical rivalry between the US and China, and NVIDIA's role in it.

I agree it's a tragedy for NVIDIA, he seems to have been exceptional as a CEO, it's just too late now.

There's probably more to it.

children.author: johnnyanmac
children.textRawHtml:
Yeah, this is pretty much peak eyeball soap opera drama kind of "tea", as they say. It has my parents talking about it, and they couldn't be less in tune wih tech and AI and GPUs. And apparently US intelligence was aware of this for over a year; they were simply told to not dig deeper.

Hanlon's razor seems to apply here, so I don't really think it's a psyop. Simply information many (top secret) parties were aware of for a while that other people who are incentivized to tell everyone eventually caught up on.

children.author: program_whiz
children.textRawHtml:
Hanlon's razor: please don't attribute malice to us poor billionaires and the intelligence community (or hold us accountable), we're just so gosh-darn incompetent.

I'm tired of hearing hanlon's razor tossed around. How about the inverse: I attribute malice if doing so makes the system better and explains your behavior. Even if you are just a fool, your actions impact others and have the same consequences of malice. I hold you to account like a criminal if you act like one.

If it's all an act, then American leadership these last 10 years has done an amazing acting job of pretending to be stupid.

Yes, there is malice in the actions. No, I don't think there was some grand conspiracy to reveal it now. That's the Hanlon's razor.

I agree. Stupidity is the reasoning for the actions being revealed, not an excuse for the actions. Even if he was "one of the good ones" I still want billionaires held accountable for crimes they do.

I just realize these dsys that these aren't some grandmasters being beaten in some political game of wit. Just people who live a fundamentally different lifestyle who never "got in trouble" because they believe money will bail them out everytime.

children.author: InsideOutSanta
children.textRawHtml:
> We can't be so gullible that we think this wasn't deliberate right?

What do you mean by "this"? One thing I agree with is that we knew about this story for months. I've read about Jensen's affair with Alice Huang and her ties to the Chinese government at least five months ago.

The thing that triggered the current reporting was the new sourcing about U.S. intelligence findings that came out in late October. So mainstream news started reporting on it once they had sources they found trustworthy.

The confusing thing, though, is not that the story suddenly became big, but why it didn't become big much earlier.
